events.title: [Server] Stop the stdio server from answering a notification it refuses
events.excerpt: A notification sent before `initialize` got a `-32600` back over stdio, but a notification must never be answered ([basic](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#notifications)). Over HTTP the refusal keeps its `400`, which the spec allows - stdio has no status to carry it, so it's only logged now. [P08]

events.title: [Server] Refuse a 2026-07-28 request with a null id instead of dropping it
events.excerpt: `StatelessProtocol` took `"id": null` for a notification and acknowledged it, so the client never got an answer. MCP forbids a null id on requests ([basic](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#requests)) and JSON-RPC only treats a missing `id` as a notification - it's refused with `-32600` now, like the handshake era already does. [P05]

events.title: [Server] Refuse a message whose `jsonrpc` version is not `2.0`
events.excerpt: Only `Request::fromArray()` and the response classes checked `jsonrpc`, so a `2026-07-28` request that `StatelessProtocol` serves without `MessageFactory` - like `subscriptions/listen` - and any handshake-era notification went through with e.g. `"jsonrpc": "1.0"`. Both are refused with `-32600` now ([basic](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#messages)). [P04]
